seal.statement: A certification verdict an existing owner already computes becomes observable by a v2 probe, without that observation becoming a second opinion. The stat gate runs the window, the summary tool classifies it and the sealed-bar file holds the population it must be drawn from; what did not exist was any way for the solver to see the answer, because the v1 sealed-bar metric is on v2's non-measuring list and the scenario-harness probe silently drops the run count, the certification flag and the sealed-bar file. A projector supplies exactly that middle and nothing else: it reads the recorded verdict and the recorded window identity, compares each against what the sealed-bar file seals, and reports what the window does not carry. It recomputes no pass rate, no interval and no classification; a verdict below the bar stays below it even where the numbers would round the other way, a bar lower than the sealed one is refused rather than adopted, and a safety breach is never outweighed by the statistics. It is generic over the scenario, so a second certification does not mean a second checker.

text: Built the projector as the missing middle and nothing more. scripts/checks/certification-verdict.js locates the newest certification aggregate for a named scenario, reads the verdict the stat gate already computed and the window identity it already recorded, and compares each against what the sealed-bar file seals; every condition it reports is a comparison between two recorded values, so it derives no pass rate, no interval and no classification of its own. Nineteen conditions cover the fourteen fields the quest's canonical-verdict-projection constraint enumerates. Three scenarios pin what it must not do: a window whose numbers would clear the bar but whose owner classified it below stays refused, an aggregate recording a bar the file does not seal is refused on both the bar and the bound rather than adopting the smaller number, and a safety breach refuses on its own. It is keyed by scenario against the sealed-bars file, so snapshot-live-rebuild is projected by naming it rather than by a second checker, and a scenario nobody sealed is refused rather than guessed at.
